purpose: Discriminate the production call topology against the exact bound EntityOS EffectGate/EffectJournal API without a real external effect or a second effect authority.
hypothesis: The current two-stage F2 authorize-then-executor port is not truthfully compatible with the bound EffectGate.execute API because EffectGate.execute owns journal begin, action execution and finalization in one call. A single-owner topology can preserve one effect authority, but exact crash-safe F2 call correlation may still require an admitted canonical correlation surface.
counterhypotheses: The bound EffectGate returns while the canonical journal is still PENDING and therefore can act as the current F2 pre-dispatch authorizer.
Recovery of a residual PENDING row can silently replay the action.
A separate F2 executor remains necessary after successful EffectGate.execute.

assertions: one EffectGate.execute performs exactly one EffectJournal.begin and returns with the effect row VERIFIED
a truthful ALLOW evidence object using the post-return journal state is rejected by the current PENDING-only two-stage F2 bridge
EffectJournal.recover_pending changes PENDING to UNKNOWN_AFTER_RESTART and a second recovery adds no effect row

next_exact_action: Run the pinned cross-repository deterministic CI. If it passes, hand the result to the active WP105 owner as a topology falsifier: retire direct EffectGate.execute-as-authorizer wiring, preserve single canonical execution ownership, and discriminate how exact F2 call identity is durably bound before a crash can lose the returned effect_id.
